newsitem.title: USA: Calif. home sales up in Oct. over year ago - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. home sales up in Oct. over year ago - report.

text.p: California home sales increased 7.7 percent in October from the 1995 rate, while year-to-date home sales registered the highest sales pace seen in the 1990s, according to a report on Monday.

The California Association of Realtors and Transamerica Corp's MetroScan real estate service said 499,370 existing, single-family detached homes closed escrow during October on a seasonally-adjusted, annualized basis.
The October sales pace increased 7.7 percent from the October 1995 annualized rate, when 463,800 homes were sold.
The October rate was down 2.7 percent from a revised annualized rate of 513,470 homes sold in September.
Year-to-date, statewide home sales have increased 21.4 percent, compared with the January through October period of 1995, the California Association of Realtors said.

"California home sales have now increased from a year ago for 13 consecutive months -- the latest sign that the state's housing market is experiencing a deep and broad-based recovery," association President Bob Kulick said.

The statewide median price of an existing, single-family detached home sold during October was $174,100, down 3.1 percent from $179,740 in September. The October median price declined 1.0 percent from October 1995.

Leslie Appleton-Young, California Association of Realtors vice president of economics and public policy, said the association expected California's housing market recovery to continue at a healthy pace into 1997.
The California Association of Realtors is one of the largest state trade associations in the United States, with nearly 100,000 members. It is headquartered in Los Angeles.
